issues.description: The controller method deletePerson has different visibility in template vs solution. In the template PersonResource.deletePerson is declared public (exposed like the other REST endpoints), whereas in the solution the same handler method is declared private. This is a structural visibility mismatch for a Spring MVC controller method and is surprising for students comparing template and solution — handler methods are typically public and having one private is inconsistent with the rest of the controller and with the template. It may confuse students about expected method visibility for REST endpoints and looks like an accidental change in the solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Restore consistent visibility for the deletePerson handler. Make the solution's deletePerson method public to match the template and the other controller methods (or conversely make the template match, but prefer public for controller handler methods). This removes the surprise/confusion and follows common Spring MVC conventions.

issues.description: The test class PersonServiceTest has differing test-configuration annotations between template and solution: the template version includes @AutoConfigureMockMvc, while the solution's PersonServiceTest omits this annotation. This is an inconsistent test configuration across artifacts and may confuse students about the intended test setup (whether MockMvc is expected/configured) when comparing template and solution test code.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the test configuration annotations between template and solution. Either add @AutoConfigureMockMvc to the solution's PersonServiceTest (if MockMvc is intended there) or remove it from the template so both artifacts document the same test setup. Documenting the intended test configuration in the problem statement can also help avoid confusion.
